> The `argparse` tree in `python/prolog_tsetlin/cli.py` owns command names, arguments, defaults, metavariables, and syntax. This page is generated from the live parser; `ptm help <topic>` and `docs/manual/reference/help-topics.md` share the conceptual topic registry.

## `ptm`

Train, inspect, search, and package deterministic PTM models.

*Conceptual help and examples: ptm help [TOPIC]*

| Argument | Help |
|---|---|
| `--version` | show program's version number and exit |

Subcommands of `ptm`:

- `ptm artifact` — inspect, verify, or run a portable .ptm artifact
- `ptm export` — freeze a scalar TM snapshot JSON file into a .ptm artifact
- `ptm export-logic` — package a fixed LogicProgram32 JSON file into a .ptm artifact
- `ptm export-pa` — package a validated Class II PA JSON artifact into a .ptm file
- `ptm help` — list or explain conceptual help topics
- `ptm search` — run a resource-bounded GNU Prolog search
- `ptm tui` — launch the optional terminal workbench

### `ptm artifact`

Export, inspect, verify, and consume deterministic .ptm artifacts.

*Concepts and examples: ptm help artifacts*

Subcommands of `ptm artifact`:

- `ptm artifact inspect` — validate and describe an artifact
- `ptm artifact run-record` — preprocess typed JSON records and run inference
- `ptm artifact verify` — check integrity, contracts, and conformance vectors

#### `ptm artifact inspect`

Export, inspect, verify, and consume deterministic .ptm artifacts.

*Concepts and examples: ptm help artifacts*

| Argument | Help |
|---|---|
| `model` | portable .ptm artifact (required) |
| `--manifest` | include the complete manifest |
| `--pretty` | indent JSON output |

#### `ptm artifact run-record`

Materialize raw typed records through an artifact's preprocessing contract.

*Concepts and examples: ptm help preprocessing*

| Argument | Help |
|---|---|
| `model` | portable .ptm artifact (required) |
| `--record JSON` | JSON object; repeat to run multiple records |
| `--jsonl PATH` | newline-delimited JSON records; use - for standard input |
| `--pretty` | indent JSON output |

### `ptm export`

Export, inspect, verify, and consume deterministic .ptm artifacts.

*Concepts and examples: ptm help artifacts*

| Argument | Help |
|---|---|
| `snapshot` | scalar TM snapshot JSON file (required) |
| `output` | destination .ptm artifact (required) |
| `--name` | artifact title; defaults to the input stem |
| `--description` | artifact description |
| `--author` | author name; repeat as needed |
| `--license` | license identifier (default: `'unspecified'`) |
| `--intended-use` | intended-use statement (default: `'research'`) |
| `--limitations` | limitations statement (default: `'research prototype'`) |
| `--feature-names` | comma-separated feature names in input order |
| `--feature-literal-ids` | comma-separated integer literal IDs |
| `--feature-catalog-version` | feature-catalog version label (default: `'anonymous-v1'`) |

### `ptm search`

Run finite, deadline-limited GNU Prolog searches and inspect their budgets.

*Concepts and examples: ptm help bounded-search*

Subcommands of `ptm search`:

- `ptm search decision-tree` — synthesize an exact bounded decision tree
- `ptm search feature-template` — select an exact typed feature template
- `ptm search repair` — repair a parent tree from counterexamples
- `ptm search ta-clause` — synthesize an exact signed TA clause
- `ptm search threshold` — find an exact monotone masked threshold

#### `ptm search decision-tree`

Run finite, deadline-limited GNU Prolog searches and inspect their budgets.

*Concepts and examples: ptm help bounded-search*

| Argument | Help |
|---|---|
| `request` | ptm.search.request.v1 JSON file |
| `--demo` | run the built-in bounded example |
| `--timeout` | override the request deadline in seconds (0.1 through 300) |
| `--gprolog` | GNU Prolog executable; otherwise use PTM_GPROLOG or PATH |
| `--pretty` | indent JSON output |
| `--output` | export fixed-Logic .ptm artifact |
| `--name` | exported artifact title |

### `ptm tui`

Explore PTM through the keyboard-first Textual workbench.

*Concepts and examples: ptm help workbench*

| Argument | Help |
|---|---|
| `--workspace` | directory used for artifacts and workbench state |
| `--demo` | initial demonstration dataset {choices: xor} (default: `'xor'`) |
| `--style` | workbench style (canonical workbench, classic compatibility shell, or single_pane compatibility alias) {choices: workbench, classic, single_pane} (default: `'workbench'`) |
